12	\paragraph{Adversarial Robustness and Transferability.}

\paragraph{Diversity--Capability Confound.}
The $r{=}0.70$ correlation between $K_{\mathrm{eff}}$ and $\eta_{\max}$ reflects a structural property: maximizing diversity requires sampling across capability tiers, introducing weaker judges (Appendix~\ref{app:diversity_capability}). Cinelli--Hazlett sensitivity analysis \citep{cinelli2020making} shows the known $\eta_{\max}$ confound exceeds $K_{\mathrm{eff}}$'s robustness value in 28/36 conditions (Appendix~\ref{app:sensitivity}), with robustness increasing with $K$ (1/12 $\to$ 3/12 $\to$ 4/12), paralleling the regime transition. The API-only subset ($r{=}0.85$) does not replicate the transition (3/12), raising the possibility that $K_{\mathrm{eff}}$ partly proxies for quantization-induced capability variance. Capability-matched subsampling ($r{=}0.50$, 9 models, 126 panels at $K{=}5$) provides partial mitigation: $K_{\mathrm{eff}}$ strengthens to 9/12 and RV exceeds $\eta_{\max}$ in 6/12 conditions (conservatively 5/12; Appendix~\ref{app:sensitivity_poolA}), versus 3/12 in the full pool. Cross-benchmark prediction ($r{\approx}0.76$--$0.78$; Appendix~\ref{app:cross_benchmark}) further supports structural rather than benchmark-specific origins. The transition is thus a descriptive regime shift whose causal attribution to diversity requires capability-controlled designs.
